doc.title: Ray Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998

title: The Depression and the family's lost real estate savings
summary: Family money in real estate was lost by 1933, but they kept some buildings and rent was covered.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: Did they ever talk much about the Depression years?

Yeah, as a matter of fact. So we’re talking about — well it didn’t really hit them until about I think it must have been ‘33, ‘34, ‘32. The crash was 1929. They had their money in real estate, and it took about — and he made good money, he had a Cadillac and he had a raccoon coat and all that. But they invested it in real estate, and the whole thing I guess, by 1933, everything was, you know mortgages foreclosed and all that kind of stuff. Yeah, I knew about that. But of course he kept working and he earned a living. But after that it wasn’t smooth sailing.

Not very much because they hung on to a couple of buildings. They were in partners with my uncle. And so there was apartments that was available to them. So that helped, that their rent was taken care of. But yeah, I remember, you know, no more Cadillacs. It was a ‘28 Cadillac I think, I remember it.
